title: The Tide-Pool Tenant
premise: A tiny landlord charges rent to every crab and makes the player mediator.
pressure: A crab landlord posts eviction notices on tidepool stones. His tenants say the new rent is a pinch of moonlight every dawn.
investigate: Read the leases before anyone gets moved
success: Each document contains the same illegible signature, dated on a day the tide never went out.
failure: A wave washes the papers away, but the landlord admits there is no dry place to relocate anyone.
help: Mediate a fair shared use of the pool
helpOutcome: The crabs keep their homes; the landlord receives a pebble marked COMMON WATER.

title: Message in a Glass Kombucha
premise: A bottle washes ashore with the player's own handwriting and tomorrow's date.
pressure: A kombucha bottle rolls up between your shoes. The letter inside, signed in your handwriting, describes a rockfall tomorrow at the point where three families are sitting today. The date is right; the explanation is not.
investigate: Compare the sketch with the cliff face and an independently posted warning
success: The tide chart leaves out an hour that appears in the bottle's margin. A local volunteer confirms the cliff is already shedding grit.
failure: The ink runs before you can preserve the time. You still know where the dangerous overhang is, which turns out to be the useful part.
help: Move people away from the unstable edge without asking them to believe you
helpOutcome: The picnic moves inland. A few pebbles begin falling where the blanket used to be. The family thanks you for the warning, not the time travel.

title: The Last Sea Glass
premise: One piece of glass contains a miniature working lighthouse.
pressure: Inside a piece of green sea glass, a lighthouse rotates with the solemnity of somebody fulfilling a very small contract. Its beam points inland, across the footprints of a collector looking for what she lost.
investigate: Trace the miniature beacon across a real map before moving the glass
success: The beam picks out a channel absent from the chart. You record the position and write UNVERIFIED in letters big enough to resist the temptation to announce a discovery.
failure: The glass slips beneath the sand. For a second the beam draws a line toward higher ground; you mark the direction, not an invented certainty.
help: Return the glass and ask whether the collector wants its secret kept
helpOutcome: The collector recognizes it as a gift from her grandmother. She agrees to show you the light, but not to surrender the glass. That seems a reasonable arrangement.

title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Second Light
premise: A phantom light warns of things not visible to boats.
pressure: A second light appears above Trinidad Head whenever a boat passes a harmless-looking patch of water. The harbor pilot refuses to name it.
investigate: Cross-check the phantom flashes with radio logs
success: The pattern predicts a submerged obstruction that ordinary instruments miss.
failure: A cloud spoils the count, but one sailor confirms the light did not track any known vessel.
help: Share the warning with local crews
helpOutcome: The harbor keeps a careful watch rather than send anyone toward an unverified beacon alone.

title: Fish with a Press Credential
premise: A salmon gives an exclusive interview in exchange for discretion.
pressure: A salmon with a press badge demands an off-record interview. It knows the migration route of a fish species not yet named.
investigate: Ask for a source that can be checked without betraying the fish
success: Its route corresponds to a blocked stream culvert whose public permit is due next month.
failure: The recorder fills with bubbling; the salmon leaves you a drawing scratched into wet sand.
help: Protect the informant's route instead of publishing a spectacle
helpOutcome: Volunteers clear litter from a tributary, and the fish returns without a headline.

title: The Harbor Below the Harbor
premise: A low tide exposes a dock that appears on no navigational chart.
pressure: At extreme low tide a second harbor opens beneath the familiar docks. Every post carries a shipping label stamped NOT YET.
investigate: Map the lower pilings against the modern waterfront
success: They match a proposed breakwater that has not passed its public hearing.
failure: The water rises before you finish; you remember an unmistakable brass mooring cleat.
help: Help a stranded visitor back to the upper dock
helpOutcome: The stranger makes it to shore with dry shoes and a warning not to buy future land on credit.

title: Fog Bank Number Seventeen
premise: A weather clerk stamps fog permits and rejects the player's identity.
pressure: A clerk at a pop-up weather window insists your name is already registered to fog bank seventeen, where you supposedly live.
success: The address is the county's missing harbor district; the expiration date is a hundred years ahead.
failure: The clerk shreds the duplicate and says you will receive the original by mail.
help: Challenge the clerk's exclusion of other travelers
helpOutcome: She opens a public queue and finally issues shelter permits to people who cannot prove a forecast.

title: Footprints Arriving from the Sea
premise: Wet tracks walk uphill before the waves arrive.
pressure: Wet footprints climb from a calm sea long before the surf can have made them. They avoid every sleeping shorebird.
investigate: Measure the track spacing before the incoming wave
success: The steps are the same distance apart across dry rock and wet sand, as if their owner is weightless.
failure: You lose the pattern at the bluff; a child keeps a sketch of the final print.
help: Guide curious hikers away from nesting birds
helpOutcome: You cordon off the fragile sand while the mysterious walker continues without an audience.

title: The Borrowed Sunset
premise: A photographer discovers the horizon belongs to next Tuesday.
pressure: A photographer has copyrighted this sunset because, she insists, it belongs to Tuesday. Her proofs show the horizon in two places at once.
investigate: Check the film timestamps against the tide
success: The second horizon matches a weather report from a future date and the wrong moon phase.
failure: The memory card corrupts, leaving one negative with an impossible sun.
help: Invite the community to witness without buying the sky
helpOutcome: The photographer projects the image at the library for free, and everyone argues productively about what they saw.

title: The Listening Cliffs
premise: A familiar voice calls from an impossible angle of rock.
pressure: A familiar voice calls from a cliff face angled away from the beach. The person it imitates is safe at home.
investigate: Find an echo path without approaching unstable rock
success: The voice comes from a narrow dry fissure containing a map in an unfamiliar coastal script.
failure: The gravel shifts and you retreat before learning the words, alive and with a reliable recording.
help: Keep other visitors back from the edge
helpOutcome: A volunteer hangs a temporary warning; nobody is lured into the drop by a voice they love.

title: Underwater Open Mic
premise: Sea creatures perform comedy whose punch lines cause harmless tremors.
pressure: Underwater comics perform through a pool of clear water. Each punchline produces a harmless tremor that makes nearby cups dance.
investigate: Count the tremors and ask who is listening
success: The sequence repeats a coastal warning code once used by an invented lighthouse keeper.
failure: Your notes dissolve when a crab steals the pen, but the rhythm can be clapped back.
help: Let the audience vote on a safer stage
helpOutcome: The performers move to a deeper pool where the comedy does not rattle the visitors' feet.

title: One Step Past the Stairs
premise: The final stair opens onto a submerged suburban porch.
pressure: The last staircase step arrives at the porch of a tidy submerged house. A doormat says WELCOME BACK and the porch light still works.
investigate: Test the water depth from a safe landing
success: The porch has a house number belonging to an unbuilt subdivision on a planning map.
failure: The light goes out before you can read the name; a dry leaf floats upward past your hand.
help: Leave a note without entering a stranger's home
helpOutcome: Someone sends the note back on a clean tide with a penciled THANK YOU.

title: The Rower Who Came Back Dry
premise: A boat returns upstream without moving the water.
pressure: A rower reaches the launch ramp upstream without having disturbed the water. The oars are soaked on one side and perfectly dry on the other.
investigate: Check the boat's wake with a second observer
success: There is a reverse current running through a strip of water narrower than an oar blade.
failure: The strip closes around your marker; the rower draws the shape in the dirt before it fades.
help: Help the exhausted rower rest and rejoin the crew
helpOutcome: The crew meets them ashore, and nobody has to prove the impossible before offering a blanket.

title: A Very Small River God
premise: A three-inch official demands bridge tolls in river pebbles.
pressure: A river god three inches high announces a toll on the Mad River bridge. His official desk is an overturned shell, and his first customer is a very worried dog.
investigate: Audit the pebbles and the water crossing
success: The toll is paying for a miniature levee that protects a real nesting bank farther downstream.
failure: The clerk refuses the audit and disappears under his desk; you still see the levee line.
help: Negotiate a free crossing for ordinary travelers
helpOutcome: The god accepts a communal bowl of pebbles and posts a new sign: NO ONE STRANDED.

title: Trail Detour to Yesterday
premise: An orange detour sign leads to the same path twenty years earlier.
pressure: An orange detour sign leads twenty years backward to a bridge still under construction. A worker recognizes your boots but not your face.
investigate: Compare the old road with the present route
success: A utility sketch marks the future location of an unexplained antenna on the bluff.
failure: The construction whistle ends the interval; you return with orange dust on an unworn sole.
help: Warn present-day cyclists about the vanished junction
helpOutcome: A temporary sign keeps riders out of the dangerous shoulder when the detour returns.

title: The Secret Tide Committee
premise: Locals with clipboards are trying to vote the moon out of office.
pressure: A secret tide committee proposes to remove the moon by popular vote. Its chair has never seen high water but owns five clipboards.
investigate: Inspect the ballots and ask what the motion would change
success: The votes are predicted tide heights, and one illegal entry points to a storm they have hidden.
failure: The chair calls a procedural recess; you rescue the agenda from the trash.
help: Invite the people who use the river to the meeting
helpOutcome: Fishers and walkers reject the cosmic stunt and vote for public flood notices instead.

title: The Kayak in the Tree
premise: An upside-down kayak drips saltwater and asks for directions home.
pressure: An upside-down kayak drips saltwater from a branch above the trail. A tiny voice beneath its seat asks if north is still north.
investigate: Follow the salt trail without shaking the tree
success: The dripping water draws an impossible estuary map across the bark.
failure: The rope breaks and the sketch washes away, though you note a new inlet.
help: Help lower the boat safely to the ground
helpOutcome: Its unseen owner thanks the rescue team and paddles it down the proper river.
